Forbidding preference over Moses after a Muslim slapped a Jew, the Prophet said that when people swoon on Resurrection Day he will rise first and find Moses holding the Throne.
Allah will grasp the earth and roll up the heavens; the earth becomes bread, and people are gathered on white land, disbelievers on their faces, all barefoot, naked and uncircumcised.
Adam will be told to bring out the people of the Fire, nine hundred ninety-nine of every thousand, yet the Prophet hopes his followers will be half of Paradise's people.
On Resurrection Day people sweat to their ears, bloodshed is judged first, wrongs are repaid from good deeds, questioned accounts mean punishment, and a disbeliever would ransom himself with gold.
Allah will speak to each person on Resurrection Day without an interpreter, the Fire facing him; shield yourselves from the Fire even with half a date or a good word.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers, faces like the full moon, will enter Paradise without reckoning, shunning branding, ruqya and omens and trusting their Lord; Ukasha asked to join them.
Once all enter Paradise or the Fire, death will be slaughtered between them and eternity announced; the Prophet saw most in Paradise were poor and most in the Fire women.
Allah will grant the people of Paradise His lasting pleasure, and the Prophet told Haritha's mother, her son martyred at Badr, there are many Paradises and he is in Firdaus.
The width between a disbeliever's two shoulders will equal the distance a fast rider covers in three days.
A rider cannot cross a Paradise tree's shade in a hundred years; seventy or seven hundred thousand enter together, faces like the full moon, seeing its lofty abodes like stars.
The Fire's least punished man has embers under his feet boiling his brain, as Abu Talib may; some come out burnt through intercession; shield yourselves even with half a date.
People will ask Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus to intercede, each declining, until Muhammad intercedes again and again, taking people out of the Fire into Paradise.
Haritha, martyred at Badr, is in Firdaus, the highest of many Paradises; a journey in Allah's Cause or a foot's space in Paradise outweighs the whole world.
Each sees his place in the other abode; the sincere monotheist wins the Prophet's intercession; the last man out of the Fire gets ten worlds; Abbas asks about Abu Talib.
Believers will see their Lord plainly as sun and moon; a hooked bridge spans the Fire, prostration marks save the burnt, and the last man pleads his way into Paradise.
The Prophet precedes his people at the Lake-Fount, a month's journey wide, its water whiter than milk, countless cups; al-Kauthar, the abundant good given him, includes a river in Paradise.
Some companions will be driven from the Prophet's Lake-Fount, he being told they innovated and turned apostate after him; in a dream he saw such groups led to the Fire.
Between the Prophet's house and pulpit is a garden of Paradise, his pulpit stands over his Lake-Fount, and he will be his people's predecessor there.
After praying over Uhud's martyrs, the Prophet said he saw his Fount and held the keys to earth's treasures, fearing not their worshipping others but their rivalry over worldly treasures.
The Lake-Fount is as wide as from Medina to Sana', its vessels countless as stars, and some will be taken from it for turning on their heels after the Prophet.
In the womb an angel writes each person's provision, lifespan and whether wretched or blessed; that writing decides his final deeds, and each finds easy what he was created for.
Asked about pagans' children dying young, the Prophet said Allah knows what they would have done; every child is born with Islamic faith, its parents making it Jew or Christian.
A woman gets only what Allah wrote for her, everything has its fixed term, coitus interruptus cannot stop an ordained soul, and the Prophet foretold everything till the Hour.
Each person's place in Fire or Paradise is assigned, yet all must act; a brave fighter the Prophet called of the Fire killed himself, deeds being judged by the last.
Vowing prevents nothing and brings nothing Allah has not written; it only draws out a miser's wealth.
On a campaign the Prophet told those shouting Takbir they call the All-Listener, All-Seer, not the deaf or absent, and taught 'La haula wala quwata illa billah', a Paradise treasure.
Every caliph has two groups of advisers, one urging good and one urging evil, and the protected one is whom Allah protects.
Allah has written each son of Adam's share of adultery: the eye's by looking, the tongue's by speech, the self's by longing, the private parts confirming or refusing it.
Ibn Abbas says the vision of verse 17.60, a trial for mankind, was what the Prophet saw with his eyes on his Night Journey, and the cursed tree is Zaqqum.
When Moses blamed Adam for turning them out of Paradise, Adam answered that Allah had written that deed forty years before creating him, and so Adam won the argument.
After prayer the Prophet said none can withhold what Allah gives or give what He withholds, and told people to seek refuge from calamity, an evil end and bad fate.
The Prophet very often swore, 'No, by Him Who turns the hearts'.
The Prophet told Ibn Saiyad he could not exceed his limits and stopped Umar killing him: if he were the Dajjal Umar could not overcome him, otherwise killing gained nothing.
Allah sent plague as punishment on whom He willed but made it mercy for believers: whoever patiently stays in a stricken town, accepting what Allah wrote, earns a martyr's reward.
At the Trench the Prophet carried earth, saying without Allah they would not have been guided, fasted or prayed, and asking for calm and firm feet against the enemy.
Whoever swears, then finds something better, should do the better and expiate, as Abu Bakr and the Prophet did; persisting in an oath harming one's family is a greater sin.
When people criticised Usama's command, the Prophet swore his father Zaid had deserved command and was among those most beloved to him, as Usama was after him.
The Prophet's oath used to be, 'No, by Him Who turns the hearts'.
The Prophet swore that once Caesar and Khosrau are ruined no Caesar or Khosrau will follow them, and that their treasures will be spent in Allah's Cause.
The Prophet swore that if his followers knew what he knows, they would weep much and laugh little.
